- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 15–30%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates downside risk; add 10–25% buffer to low forecasts.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 2x prior peak or 1.5x recent high.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment spikes, model underreacts; increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment drops.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply exponential decay to recent highs/lows (e.g., 0.85 decay factor).
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 day sentiment shift.
- If forecast is >2.5x true outcome for 3 consecutive days, apply downward correction rule: subtract 0.25x forecast from next 3 days’ predictions.
